MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  FEBRUARY 24, 2026

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR ZERUNYAN called the meeting to order at 7:04 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Karin Conklin, Vice President, Membership of the Palos Verdes Peninsula Chamber
of Commerce.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN presented a certificate of recognition to Vice President Karin Conklin
and incoming Board Chair Ryan Halvorsen, who accepted the certificate on behalf of the
Chamber in honor of its 70th anniversary.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  Schmitz

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Attorney Steve McEwen
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Development/PW Director Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING MARCH 2026 AS WOMEN'S HISTORY MONTH

MAYOR ZERUNYAN declared March 2026 as Women’s History Month, and presented the
proclamation to Nancy Mahr, President of the Palos Verdes Peninsula League of Women
Voters.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-H AS FOLLOWS
  BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  APPROVED.

B.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT OF JANUARY 2026

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

C.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF JANUARY 2026

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 9, 2026

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
FEBRUARY 24, 2026
   RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 10, 2026

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

F.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 10, 2026

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

G.  PALOS VERDES PENINSULA PUBLIC SAFETY COMMITTEE & REGIONAL
  CONTRACT LAW COMMITTEE MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 13, 2025

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

H.  2025 CITY CELEBRATION DEBRIEF

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

A.  WASTE MANAGEMENT "RECYCLING HERO" QUARTERLY DRAWING FOR ONE
  YEAR OF FREE RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL REFUSE SERVICE

  COMMERCIAL: 655 Deep Valley Drive
  RESIDENTIAL: 13 Mystery Acres Road

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

None.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  USER FEE REVISIONS - PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2616, amending the
  Community Development and Public Works Department Fees and Charges for Fiscal
  Year 2025-26 with respect to the Encroachment Permit processing fees and the
  Highway/Road Permit inspection fees.

Community Development & Public Works Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per
the agenda material).

Director Naughton confirmed there were approximately 130 encroachment permits issued
in the last year, and overcharges are still being calculated, in response to COUNCIL
MEMBER STEGURA.

Director Naughton also noted that the permit processing fee most affected the utility
Southern California Edison.

Director Naughton explained that Matrix Consulting Group helped to build the model, but
was not responsible for the error in the user fees.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2616, AMENDING THE COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT AND PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT FEES AND
  CHARGES FOR FISCAL YEAR 2025-26 WITH RESPECT TO THE

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
FEBRUARY 24, 2026
   ENCROACHMENT  PERMIT  PROCESSING  FEES  AND  THE
  HIGHWAY/ROAD PERMIT INSPECTION FEES.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

City Clerk Pettit read Resolution No. 2616 by title.

B.  TASK ORDER AMENDMENT WITH WILLDAN ENGINEERING FOR ADDITIONAL
  ENGINEERING, CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT, AND INSPECTION SERVICES
  FOR THE PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AT DAPPLEGRAY SCHOOL PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve Task Order 2026-16 amendment to
  Task Order Dated August 25, 2020, under Willdan’s Engineering’s Master Professional
  Services Agreement, increasing the not-to-exceed amount from $250,492 by
  $37,216.25 for a total of $287,708.25 for construction management and inspection
  services, all to the satisfaction of the City Attorney.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN noted that staff requested to remove item from agenda, to be
reconsidered at the next City Council meeting.

  POSTPONED TO A FUTURE MEETING.

C.  AUTHORIZATION TO SOLICIT CONSTRUCTION BIDS FOR THE PALOS VERDES
  DRIVE NORTH AT DAPPLEGRAY SCHOOL PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize staff to solicit competitive
  construction bids for the Palos Verdes Drive North at Dapplegray School project and
  direct staff to return to City Council with the bid results and a recommended action
  for construction contract award.

Community Development & Public Works Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per
the agenda material).

Director Naughton noted that the City received additional Measure M funding to help support
this project, and will return to the City Council with updated Metro Funding agreements, in
response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  AYOR PRO TEM SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AUTHORIZE STAFF TO SOLICIT COMPETITIVE CONSTRUCTION BIDS
  FOR THE PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AT DAPPLEGRAY SCHOOL
  PROJECT AND DIRECT STAFF TO RETURN TO CITY COUNCIL WITH THE
  BID RESULTS AND A RECOMMENDED ACTION FOR CONSTRUCTION
  CONTRACT AWARD.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

9.  OLD BUSINESS

None.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
FEBRUARY 24, 2026
 11.  CITY COUNCIL / REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA stated that she will be attending the Los Angeles County
Sheriff’s Department’s Contract City Council Academy over next several months, beginning
with a ride-along Thursday night.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF announced an upcoming event hosted by Cal Cities on March 25,
“Government Connections Networking Seminar.”

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHACHTER attended the Los Angeles County Sanitation District Board
meeting this month.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS
None.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

None.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

MAYOR ZERUNYAN adjourned the meeting at 7:34 p.m. to Tuesday, March 24, 2026 at
7:00 p.m. for the purpose of a regular meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit, City Clerk  Frank V. Zerunyan, Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
FEBRUARY 24, 2026
